device.model: ur3_moveit MoverService (MoveIt, OMPL) of the Unity robotics object-pose-estimation demo
device.name: UR3 pick-and-place planner (Unity object pose estimation demo)

facts.text: mover.py's moveit_server initialises moveit_commander and the ur3_moveit_server node and advertises the service ur3_moveit of type MoverService with the callback plan_pick_and_place.
MoverService takes UR3MoveitJoints joints_input, a geometry_msgs/Pose pick_pose and a geometry_msgs/Pose place_pose, and returns a moveit_msgs/RobotTrajectory[] named trajectories.
UR3MoveitJoints carries six float64 joint values joint_00 to joint_05 and its own pick_pose and place_pose.
moveit_msgs/RobotTrajectory holds a trajectory_msgs/JointTrajectory joint_trajectory and a trajectory_msgs/MultiDOFJointTrajectory multi_dof_joint_trajectory.
The planner's joint names are shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint and wrist_3_joint.
plan_pick_and_place converts joint_00 to joint_05 of the request from degrees to radians with math.radians to form the start configuration.
plan_trajectory sets the start state to the given joint angles, sets the destination pose as the pose target and returns the result of move_group.plan().
Under Python 3, planCompat returns element 1 of the tuple that plan() returns.
plan_pick_and_place appends five plans, pre grasp, grasp, pick up, place and post place, each starting at the last point of the previous one, clears the pose targets and returns the response.
The grasp plan targets the pick pose lowered by 0.075 in z; the comment calls it a static value coming from Unity.
The post-place plan targets the place pose raised by 0.075 in z.
plan_pick_and_place first calls setup_scene.

setup_scene assigns a new MoveGroupCommander for the group arm to the module-global move_group, creates a PlanningSceneInterface and a RobotCommander, sleeps 2 s and adds a box named table of size (1.2, 1.8, 0.01) at z -0.02+0.77 in the planning frame.
The docstring says gripper behaviour is handled outside this trajectory planning: the gripper closes after the grasp position and opens after the place position.
The SRDF defines the group arm as the chain from base_link to ee_link.
The SRDF's default group state of arm sets all six arm joints to 0.
pose_est.launch loads params.yaml, includes demo.launch and starts server_endpoint.py, pose_estimation_script.py and mover.py.
demo.launch loads ur3_with_gripper.urdf as robot_description, includes ros_controllers.launch, spawns arm_controller and starts move_group.launch.
move_group.launch defaults allow_trajectory_execution to true and fake_execution to false.
ros_controllers.yaml lists one controller with an empty name, action_ns follow_joint_trajectory, type FollowJointTrajectory and the six arm joints.
The documentation says the launch may report that the controller spawner process died and that this is safe to ignore once the final message is Ready to plan.
server_endpoint.py starts the ROS-TCP TcpServer with three routes: a UR3Trajectory subscriber, the ur3_moveit service as ur3_moveit, and the pose_estimation_service service as pose_estimation_srv.
The ROS-TCP endpoint reads its ROS_IP, ROS_TCP_PORT (default 10000), UNITY_IP and UNITY_SERVER_PORT (default 5005) parameters.
The ROS-TCP endpoint's client thread reads one message per connection, routes it by destination name and, for a service, sends the response back on that connection and closes it.
The ROS-TCP endpoint's RosService calls the ROS service up to three times on a ServiceException and returns None after any other exception.

Unity's PublishJoints builds the MoverService request from the arm's current joint targets, the estimated cube position plus a pick offset and the goal position plus a place offset, and sends it to rosServiceName with TrajectoryResponse as the callback.
TrajectoryPlanner's public field rosServiceName defaults to ur3_moveit.
Unity's CurrentJointConfig fills joint_00 to joint_05 from the xDrive targets of the six arm articulation bodies.
TrajectoryPlanner's fixed values are a 0.06 s joint assignment wait, a 0.5 s pose assignment wait, a gripper angle of 14, a pick offset of 0.255 and a place offset of 0.275 in Unity's y axis.
TrajectoryResponse starts the ExecuteTrajectories coroutine when the response holds trajectories and otherwise logs an error and re-enables the buttons.

ExecuteTrajectories writes each point's positions, converted with Rad2Deg, as the xDrive targets of the arm joints, waits after each point, closes the gripper after the grasp plan and opens it after the place plan.
The pose estimation button handler captures the camera image and invokes the pose estimation service.
InvokePoseEstimationService builds a sensor_msgs Image with encoding RGBA from the render texture and sends a PoseEstimationServiceRequest to pose_estimation_srv.
pose_estimation_script.py advertises pose_estimation_service of type PoseEstimationService.
PoseEstimationService takes a sensor_msgs/Image image and returns a geometry_msgs/Pose estimated_pose.
_save_image writes each request image as a numbered PNG (Input<count>.png) under the package's images directory, creating the directory when it is missing.
The documentation runs roslaunch ur3_moveit pose_est.launch, then Play in Unity, then the Pose Estimation button; MoveIt returns trajectories to Unity, where the poses are executed.
The documented container publishes ports 10000 and 5005.
The Docker image builds from ros:noetic-ros-base.
The Docker image installs ros-noetic-moveit and ros-noetic-rosbridge-suite among its apt packages.
The Docker image copies the moveit_msgs, robotiq, ros_tcp_endpoint, universal_robot and ur3_moveit packages into the catkin workspace.

determinism.notes: The fake answers a fixed placeholder plan shape; MoveIt's OMPL planning in a live deployment is randomized and its plans differ between calls

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS recording fake of the ur3_moveit MoverService (no MoveIt, OMPL or Unity)
gaps: PLAN ONLY: the package never executes a plan
in the upstream pipeline only Unity executes trajectories, and only those answering its own request, so a receipt never shows motion of the simulated arm

the fake's plans are straight joint-space segments through invented configurations; it models only the response shape, the five-plan order, the chaining of each plan's start to the previous plan's end, the start configuration taken from the request in degrees and returned in radians, and the service failures; it runs no MoveIt, OMPL, collision checking or time parameterization
a live planning call first adds the same table box to MoveIt's planning scene and sleeps 2 s (mover.py:112-126); a plan that MoveIt cannot find makes the callback raise and the call fail

concurrent planning calls (from Unity or another client) share the node's module-global MoveGroupCommander, which every call replaces (mover.py:112-116), so their start states and targets can interleave, and Unity executes whatever plan answers its own request: a call that overlaps Unity's own planning can change what the simulated arm does; the package serialises only its own calls and cannot see Unity's

every input bound is operator_required (the clone states the UR3 joint limits only in radians and no workspace or quaternion bound): without the operator's overlay every call is refused LIMITS_UNSET; within it, a configuration MoveIt cannot reach still fails the plan, which is then a failed receipt
the pose estimation service, the ROS-TCP endpoint, the Unity scene with its arm, gripper, cube and camera, and the vendored universal_robot and robotiq driver stacks are NOT COVERED
the operator runs rosbridge (rosbridge_server's websocket, installed by the upstream image) next to pose_est.launch and publishes its port; the upstream documents only ports 10000 and 5005

safe_state.description: Plan-only package: it sends nothing that executes a plan or commands the Unity arm, its gripper or any controller. An e-stop latches this endpoint in software and refuses further planning requests; a planning request already sent is not awaited. It does not reach a pick-and-place that Unity started from its own Pose Estimation button: that runs in Unity's coroutine and stops only in the Unity editor.
